title: 4 · Hex bolt head: 3D die fill and flash
level: Intermediate · 3D · built-in die set · a few minutes per run
summary: A 1" bar upset into the head of a 1"-8 hex bolt (1-1/2" across flats) with a flash land sized to the ASM guidance: a non-axisymmetric part that only a 3D model can predict.
instructions: 1. The bottom die holds the Ø1" × 1-1/2" shank in a bore; the top die carries the hex head (3° draft) and a flash land with a gutter beyond it: 2 mm (about 5/64") thick and 1/4" wide (about 5.8 mm flat, w/t 2.9), on the thick side of industry practice for a 0.3 kg steel forging (ASM survey: about 1.4 mm). The isothermal model gives steadier loads with a thicker flash. Quarter model (the part is symmetric about both side planes); the dies are exact flat and cylindrical faces. The bar stands in the bore and its free end is upset into the head.
2. Press Solve. Turn Cut-away on (View ▾) to see the material flowing out of the bar into the hex.
3. Watch the fill curve: the round upset reaches the flats first; the hex corners fill last, as flash spreads over the land and the load climbs steeply.
4. Use Ctrl+5 (top view) and the slider to watch the corners fill and the flash form. F refits the view.
5. Run its multi-run over temperature and compare peak load and final fill: corner fill against flash load is the trade-off of the process.
